input.quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 selects New York law, which is our preferred governing law, and there is no arbitration clause or foreign venue anywhere in the Agreement (searches for court, venue, jurisdiction, dispute and arbitration return no other responsive text). However, the Agreement contains no dispute forum provision at all, so neither the preferred element (exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County) nor the fallback forum element is satisfied; that is a full checklist element, not a minor sub-element. We therefore target the preferred level: New York law is already met, and we add only the missing exclusive New York County venue sentence immediately after Section 10.5, leaving the governing-law sentence intact.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.

proposal.summary: Add exclusive New York County venue to the New York governing law clause.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is already governed by New York law, but it is silent on forum. We have added exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, consistent with our playbook position.

ops.text: Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York over any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement.
